event.summary: Rename stays enabled for sessions whose environment is being deleted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa

TLDR: A session can show that its sandbox or container is being deleted while still offering a working Rename editor. Submitting the edit sends a request to the unavailable environment and leaves the user in an error state.

Details: This commit introduces environment_deleting at row.rs:1179-1184 and uses it to disable Clone and Delete, while frozen withholds Stop/Restart/Replace. It omits Rename: row.rs:2671-2716 renders Rename whenever controls.rename is true and checks busy alone at 2684/2707. controls is derived only from offers_mark_seen at 1401-1402. list/view.rs:6312-6317 computes busy from client-owned requests/questions, not the environment host phase; a failed automatic sealed-environment destruction (or destruction from another client) holds none of those session claims. on_rename_start at list/view.rs:3850-3888 admits that row, and on_rename_submit at 3909-3945 sends rename_session; neither checks the environment deleting phase. SessionOps::busy_now (session_ops.rs:178-179) checks only held/questions, confirming it does not supply the omitted guard.

Contract: SPEC.md, Sandbox sessions, lines 1521-1523: "While that runs, and if it fails, Hosts and the sidebar attention area show the sandbox as being deleted, with the reason and **Retry**, and its sessions show as being deleted with their actions unavailable." Container sessions at SPEC.md:4867 inherits that contract. SPEC_impl.md:6648-6649 repeats that while a host is Deleting its sessions have actions unavailable. The concrete route is a retained session row after sealed destruction fails, already represented by being_deleted(host) returning Some(true), with no client session operation pending. At minimum the Rename dialog opens and offers a request the environment cannot serve; no data loss or security impact is established. Apply the same deleting guard to Rename presentation/admission as to the other lifecycle controls.

Suggested bucket: other (unavailable action incorrectly offered; no established material or destructive consequence). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis, not observed execution. Could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Caveat: backend refusal remains expected and prevents mutation; this finding is the incorrect available control/editor, not a claim that Rename succeeds on a sealed supervisor. Lead f1 is now closed as a finding.

event.summary: Rename stays enabled for retained sessions while their environment is being deleted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa

TLDR: A retained session row can show that its sandbox or container is being deleted while still opening an enabled Rename editor. The editor can submit a request that the helm refuses because that environment has no routable connection. The established issue is the offered unavailable editor, not a successful mutation.

Details: Synthesis confirms the full availability/admission route. row_control_visibility at row.rs:144-150 sets rename=true unconditionally for ordinary non-retired rows. The new environment_deleting flag at :1179-1184 guards Clone/Delete, while frozen covers Stop/Restart/Replace; Rename at :2671-2716 checks only busy (:2684/:2707). list/view.rs:6312-6317 derives busy from local pending/held/questions. on_rename_start at :3850-3888 checks retired_row, local busy/questions and an existing editor, but never host phase. retired_row at :1249-1255 checks only retired-container compatibility. on_rename_submit at :3909-3945 checks the editor generation/unavailable flag and begin_row_op; begin_row_operation at :868-876 checks only local questions/claims/pending before reserving. listed_rename_unavailable is reconciled only against authoritative source absence at :2250-2262, not the Deleting host phase. Thus a row still displayed with no local request/confirmation can open and submit Rename.

The failed sealed-destruction premise is preserved and bounded precisely: manager.rs:2610-2619 notes a seal independently of any GUI session claim; sessions/sandbox.rs:290-304 records an attempt and failure; manager.rs:2639-2679 retains Failed(reason) as HostState::Deleting, and :2210-2228 exposes no client whatever the actor's connection does. finish_seal runs in the helm-owned finisher (:339-360), not a page's SessionOps. hosts.rs:1537-1545 returns on provider destruction failure before deleting the registered host/cache at :1550-1554. While a cached session row remains displayed after that failure, no failed sealed-host reconnection can make its Rename request routable. A later successful supervisor refresh may show the final session already gone and remove its row; this finding does not assert that a failed destruction always leaves a session row forever. The same omission is visible while a host-level whole-environment destruction holds Deleting at hosts.rs:1513-1534 and a cached session row remains, without a session-local GUI claim.

Backend boundary: manager.status removes the client for every seal record (:2220-2224), and sessions::route_session at :905-926 refuses status.client=None with Conflict. An attempted rename is therefore refused before reaching the sealed supervisor. This prevents mutation and limits the effect to an invalid available control, an editor and its refusal.

Contract: SPEC.md:1521-1523 explicitly covers both active and failed destruction: "While that runs, and if it fails, Hosts and the sidebar attention area show the sandbox as being deleted, with the reason and **Retry**, and its sessions show as being deleted with their actions unavailable." Container sessions at :4867 inherits that rule. SPEC_impl.md:6639-6648 says seal state must preserve Deleting/no-client across holds/releases/reconnects and that Deleting sessions' actions are unavailable. No Rename/metadata exception is stated for this phase. A host-phase guard in Rename presentation and local admission should match the other unavailable lifecycle controls.

Suggested bucket: other, preserving the original offered-editor/refusal consequence. Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis for retained displayed rows; no execution observed. Could-be-highest: no established security/loss-of-work route. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none known. Material caveats: a local Delete claim can independently disable Rename while it is pending, so the failure/helm-finisher/other-client or host-level path matters; disappearance of the cached row ends the opportunity. No mutation, data loss, permanent retained row or runtime reproduction is claimed.

event.summary: Delete scope remains bound to the answered question across connection changes
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa

TLDR: Considered whether a session-only Delete could silently become deletion of the whole sandbox or container after connection loss. The source prevents that widening.

Details: row.rs:1171-1176 derives the current environment scope at render, which initially looked dangerous when a narrower confirmation remains open. But row.rs:1227-1250 chooses the displayed consequence from the rendered question token's Delete versus DeleteWhole key, not the newly computed scope. The confirming render passes that token, its guard and environment facts at 2530-2539. list/view.rs:3287-3300 first consumes precisely that opening, then uses token.key().answered(environment). shared.rs:135-148 overwrites scope from the answered key: Delete always Session, DeleteWhole always Whole. The live connection cannot turn Session into Whole. list/view.rs:3022-3055 handles an Unasked reply by opening a distinct DeleteWhole question rather than sending it. This satisfies SPEC_impl.md:1071-1090, Answers bind to what was drawn, and SPEC.md:1526-1536, requiring a warned whole-environment confirmation when the environment cannot answer.

Suggested bucket if it were present: highest, since an unwarned widened Delete could destroy other sessions and files. Could-be-highest: yes (considered consequence), but source refutes the route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: source refutation; separate question keys and answered-scope override prevent the suspected destructive widening. No specification exception is needed. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. No runtime behavior was observed.

event.summary: An old stale listing can forget a successful Restart before showing its run
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

TLDR: After restarting an interrupted session, opening it again can show the interrupted-session recovery card instead of its new terminal if a delayed listing from the earlier host outage lands after Restart succeeds. A later fresh status read corrects it.

Details: This commit removes restart_listing_floor and the listing generation argument. read_confirms_run at session_ops.rs:79-80 returns true for any stale row, even Interrupted; restarts_retired_by at 91-107 then retires remembered success whenever no request is pending. The stated reasoning at 73-76 overlooks the stale disjunct: an old Interrupted row DOES retire the outcome when stale is true. list/view.rs:1935-1953 commits such a listing if newer than the last applied read, not newer than Restart; 1976-1985 calls retirement. Restart completion at 3416-3419 records success, asks the surface reader for a refresh, then releases pending. That refresh does not fence the outstanding listing: request_listing at 2473-2474 calls reader::request_read, whose single-flight request at reader.rs:644-660 coalesces the refresh behind an existing read. ReadGate::accept_success at ops.rs:182-187 accepts the old read if it beats the last applied generation. Thus an ordinary delayed GET from the preceding outage may land after the successful POST, now see pending empty, and clear restart_succeeded. The removed floor specifically excluded reads already started at completion.

A concrete source route is an interrupted session cached during an outage: a stale listing snapshot is in flight; the host reconnects and a user Restart succeeds; that old listing completes after pending is released. The next connected listing may still say Interrupted because session_cache::merged_status preserves definite status when the Restart reply is Unknown (session_cache.rs:143-150), until the awakened supervisor refresh produces definite new liveness.
